answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock $100 for 30 days to receive one job slot per hour, whether it controls a lantern or operates a beacon. Creating more names grants no free capacity: 10,000 fake agents require $1 million locked across the same 30-day horizon. The bond is refundable, but the attacker loses access to that capital and its potential yield, making mass identity creation costly even when accounts are free.
